Source: https://langfuse.com/integrations/native/opentelemetry, opened 2026-10-07 (HTTP 200; quoted sentences confirmed on the published page), and read in full from its public docs source, github.com/langfuse/langfuse-docs @ dbc5c71946a20b44d2844992d010362469039b76 (2026-10-07), content/integrations/native/opentelemetry/index.mdx.
Each rule below quotes the sentence it comes from in its 'doc' field. VERIFIED = the quoted sentence was read in that file; nothing here is UNVERIFIED.

Finding recorded by this fixture: the documented observation input/output mapping reads langfuse.observation.input, gen_ai.prompt, input.value (OpenInference) and gen_ai.tool.call.arguments/result, and the documented user mapping reads user.id. Our otel_genai profile sends chat content as gen_ai.input.messages/gen_ai.output.messages and the user as enduser.id, which the doc does not list (they land in metadata.attributes). The openinference profile sends input.value/output.value and user.id, so it is the profile to choose for Langfuse.

transport.doc: Please note that Langfuse currently supports OTLP over HTTP with both `HTTP/JSON` and `HTTP/protobuf`. `gRPC` is not supported yet. ... the trace endpoint is `/api/public/otel/v1/traces`.

span.doc: Missing timestamps are filled in. If `startTimeUnixNano` or `endTimeUnixNano` is missing or unparseable, Langfuse copies the remaining edge ... Send both fields on every span. (traceId/spanId: the OTLP/HTTP JSON encoding, lowercase hex, which Langfuse accepts as HTTP/JSON.) Timestamps are nanoseconds: 19 digits for any date from 2001 to 2286, so a millisecond or second value fails.

forbiddenKeySegments.doc: Attribute keys that contain `__proto__`, `constructor`, or `prototype` as a path segment ... are silently dropped during ingestion.

everySpanOfASession.doc: certain trace-level attributes should be propagated to **all spans** ... `sessionId` (via `langfuse.session.id` or `session.id`)

llm.doc: model: `gen_ai.request.model`, `gen_ai.response.model` ...; usage: `gen_ai.usage.*`; type: inferred from other conventions (for example `gen_ai.operation.name`), then from a model attribute (`generation`)

tool.doc: input: ... `gen_ai.tool.call.arguments` (OpenTelemetry GenAI tool spans, used when no other input attribute is set); output: ... `gen_ai.tool.call.result`

everySpanOfASession.doc: `userId` (via `langfuse.user.id` or `user.id`); `sessionId` (via `langfuse.session.id` or `session.id`) ... need to be present on each span in the trace
